blocks.content: 1. CONCEPT OF HUMAN DEVELOPMENT

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Human Development focuses on expanding capabilities and freedoms, a concept pioneered by Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen.
The Global Human Development Index (HDI) is published annually by UNDP based on Health, Education, and Standard of Living.
NITI Aayog releases India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) utilizing National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data.
India is classified under the 'Medium Human Development' category with an HDI score of 0.644.
India's demographic dividend window spans from 2005 to 2055, requiring substantial strategic investments via Skill India and public health infrastructure.

blocks.content: Human Development refers to the process of enlarging people’s choices and improving their quality of life. It focuses not merely on income growth but on expanding human capabilities such as living a long and healthy life, acquiring knowledge and achieving a decent standard of living.
The concept was popularised by economist Mahbub-ul-Haq and further developed by Amartya Sen’s ‘Capability Approach’, which emphasises freedom and opportunities.
2. HUMAN DEVELOPMENT INDEX (HDI)
HDI is a composite index published by UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) to measure average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development.
HDI values range from 0 to 1. Countries are classified as Low, Medium, High and Very High Human Development.
3. MULTIDIMENSIONAL POVERTY INDEX (MPI)
MPI measures multiple deprivations faced by people in health, education and living standards.
It includes indicators such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, housing and assets.
4. STATUS OF HUMAN DEVELOPMENT IN INDIA

India has improved in life expectancy, literacy rate and poverty reduction over the decades. However, challenges remain in malnutrition, healthcare quality, gender inequality and regional disparities.

Major Concerns:

• Malnutrition among children

• Learning outcomes in schools

• Unemployment among youth

• Rural-urban inequality
5. EDUCATION IN INDIA
Education is a key driver of human development. Higher literacy leads to higher productivity and income.

Major Initiatives:

• Right to Education (RTE) Act

• Samagra Shiksha

• Mid-Day Meal Scheme (PM POSHAN)

• National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
Challenges include dropout rates, digital divide and quality of education.
Human development is a process of enlarging people's choices, enhancing capabilities, and expanding freedoms.
6. HEALTH IN INDIA
Health determines productivity and life expectancy. Improved healthcare reduces mortality rates.

Major Schemes:

• Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY)

• National Health Mission (NHM)

• Universal Immunization Programme

Key Indicators:

• Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)

• Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)

• Life Expectancy
7. POVERTY AND INEQUALITY
Poverty is a major obstacle to human development. India uses poverty lines and MPI to measure deprivation.
Inequality is measured using the Gini Coefficient. Higher inequality reduces inclusive growth.
8. DEMOGRAPHIC DIVIDEND
India has one of the largest working-age populations. If provided with education and skills, this can boost economic growth. However, without employment opportunities, it may lead to unemployment.

blocks.content: 9. ROLE OF GOVERNMENT IN HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
Government invests in health, education, nutrition and skill development to improve HDI.

Examples:

• Skill India Mission

• Digital India

• Poshan Abhiyaan
10.HUMAN DEVELOPMENT ADVANCED ADD-ON
1. LATEST HDI RANKING & TREND
As per the latest Human Development Report released by UNDP (recent report), India falls in the 'Medium Human Development' category with rank around 134 globally.
Trend shows gradual improvement over time, though pandemic caused temporary decline.
2. EDUCATION & HEALTH EXPENDITURE TREND (% OF GDP)
Education expenditure target is 6% of GDP (as recommended by NEP 2020). Health expenditure target is 2.5% of GDP under National Health Policy.
3. SKILL INDIA & DEMOGRAPHIC DIVIDEND LINKAGE

items: UNDP calculates HDI using four sub-indicators: Life Expectancy at Birth, Expected Years of Schooling, Mean Years of Schooling, and GNI per capita (PPP).
NITI Aayog's National MPI incorporates 12 indicators, adding Maternal Health and Bank Accounts to the standard 10 global MPI indicators.
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 sets a target public expenditure on education at 6% of GDP.

blocks.content: India has one of the youngest populations in the world. The demographic dividend refers to economic growth potential arising from a large working-age population.
Skill India Mission was launched to enhance employability of youth through skill development programs.
Major Components of Skill Development:

• Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)

• National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)

• Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)

• Apprenticeship Programs

Linkage Explanation:

• Young population + Proper skill training = Higher productivity

• Higher productivity = Higher GDP growth

• Without skills, demographic dividend may turn into demographic burden (unemployment).
RRB HIGH-VALUE SUMMARY POINTS

• India is in Medium Human Development category.

• Education target = 6% of GDP.

• Health target = 2.5% of GDP.

• Skill India converts demographic dividend into economic growth.

• HDI has 3 components: Health, Education and Income.

• HDI is published by UNDP.

• MPI measures multiple deprivations.

• Demographic dividend can accelerate growth.

• Education and health are core pillars of human development.
